That's what Spanish coach Daniel believes after coming to Xinjiang's Kashgar, where kids play football on the streets and passion for the game is everywhere.

What has he discovered about football and the kids in this city?

description: At the request of Myanmar authorities, 53 firefighters from Dehong, southwest China's Yunnan Province, crossed the border with 14 emergency vehicles on Wednesday to tackle a blaze at a gas station storing large quantities of gasoline in Muse. author: New China TV
description:
Japanese telecom operator #KDDI has acknowledged that its subsidiary #Mobicom could be responsible for the large-scale wildfire that scorched #Mongolia's protected nature reserve earlier this month.
The blaze destroyed over 528,700 hectares of land -- an area which, according to media, was more than TWICE the size of #Tokyo. The reserve is one of eastern Mongolia's best-preserved natural ecosystems, providing habitat for a wide range of wildlife, including endangered and rare species.
Local media alleged that the Japanese executives who sparked the fire had entered the restricted area for ILLEGAL FISHING.
title: Japanese firm admits sparking massive Mongolian wildfire

title: 75-year-old donates over 45,000 USD from collecting scrap

author: New China TV
description:
Why does the Long March still inspire after 90 years?

From 1934 to 1936, the Chinese Red Army crossed raging rivers, climbed snow-covered mountains and trekked through vast grasslands - while facing hunger, cold and constant enemy pursuit.

The destination changed. The road was uncertain. But the march continued.

For many Chinese, the Long March is more than a chapter of history. It has come to stand for perseverance, conviction and the courage to keep moving when the way forward is unclear.

In this episode of #DearWord, we look at how a historic journey became an enduring spirit.

#LongMarch #China
title: Dear Word | Why Does the LONG MARCH Still Inspire After 90 Years?

author: New China TV
description:
Join us on a journey through Yan’an in northwest China’s Shaanxi Province -- from Wuqi to Fenghuang Mountain, Yangjialing and Baota Mountain, then onward to Nanniwan and Yan’an New Area. Along the way, explore revolutionary history and see how the city is changing, before taking in the dramatic landscapes of Hukou Waterfall and the Yellow River’s Qiankun Bay.
This year marks the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March. From 1934 to 1936, the Red Army’s arduous journey helped lay the foundation for the eventual victory of the Chinese revolution. #LongMarch
title: LIVE: Retracing the Long March, exploring Yan’an, Shaanxi Province

author: New China TV
description:
Join us for a breathtaking aerial journey over Yudu and Ruijin in Jiangxi, China, where history and modern development meet.
From the banks of the Yudu River, where the Central Red Army began its historic Long March, to the evolving cityscape of Ruijin, our drone cameras capture the landmarks, urban neighborhoods, and rural landscapes that tell the story of a revolutionary past and a vibrant present.
Discover how these historic revolutionary heartlands are embracing new opportunities while preserving their rich heritage. Through sweeping aerial views of changing landscapes, experience the enduring spirit of the Long March and its continued legacy in modern China.  #LongMarch #RedCulture (recorded)
title: LIVE: Aerial Yudu — Retracing the starting point of the Long March

description: Xingfu Town in China's Shandong accounts for more than 40% of China's commercial kitchenware market, and local manufacturers are actively expanding into global markets.
